title: Invited: Enhancing Test Quality by Targeting Timing Marginalities Due to Process Variations
problem: Current IC test methodologies based on stuck-at and single-defect fault models miss timing failures caused by random process variations in threshold voltages that affect multiple devices simultaneously, particularly in advanced technologies.
motivation: Random process variations at advanced nodes significantly impact circuit behavior under specific operating conditions and can cause field failures not caught by conventional test methods targeting passive defects.
method: Instead of testing for individual broken transistors (the traditional approach), this methodology designs tests to catch timing slowdowns from random manufacturing variations in transistor threshold voltages—the voltage levels that control when transistors turn on. When multiple performance-critical transistors drift the same way due to manufacturing randomness, the chip becomes just barely too slow to work, even though no single component is defective. The tests target these correlated multi-transistor variations directly, rather than assuming transistors either work perfectly or fail completely.
key_novelty: Instead of testing for single broken transistors, the methodology targets timing failures caused by random manufacturing variations in transistor threshold voltages that affect multiple devices together.
contributions: Analysis of timing failures caused by random threshold voltage variations in advanced technologies
Methodology for developing reliable tests targeting multi-device process variation effects
Framework for prioritizing performance-sensitive device parameters in test generation
Demonstration that conventional test methods miss variation-induced timing failures

metrics.test_coverage: detection of timing failures from process variations

baselines: conventional stuck-at and single-defect test methodologies
primary_theme: Variation-aware IC testing for process-induced timing failures
